calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Blues are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Predators are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Blues.
calls.call: The Blues’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Predators.

calls.head: The Predators want O'Reilly head to head with Thomas
calls.body: At home, the Predators keep sending O'Reilly’s line (Stamkos, O'Reilly and Kerfoot) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Andrew Brunette has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Blues’ first line is Thomas, Holloway and Snuggerud.

NSH.head: We had Nashville as slight underdogs (43%), and they pulled it off.

STL.head: We leaned St. Louis’s way (57%), but Nashville had other ideas.

surprises.head: Nashville found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Nashville usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots, and St. Louis is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Not tonight: Nashville’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 5.8% (about 5.4% against St. Louis) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: The Predators beat the Blues
paras: Philip Broberg got the scoring started for the Blues early in the first. Jonathan Marchessault tied it up for Nashville on a penalty shot a little over two minutes later. Filip Forsberg put the Predators up 2-1 less than four minutes later, and Adam Edström made it 3-1 shorthanded midway through the second. Jimmy Snuggerud cut Nashville’s lead to 3-2 on the power play 31 seconds later, but that was as close as they got. Ryan O'Reilly stretched the lead to 4-2 early in the third, and Jack Drury scored his first goal for Nashville midway through the period to make it 5-2.

The Predators drove the play, and the scoreboard caught up. Juuse Saros made 24 saves for the Predators, and Jordan Binnington allowed five goals on 24 shots. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Adam Wilsby, by our Swing measure. The Preds moved to 3-2-3, and the Blues fell to 3-4-1.

items.text: The Predators won for the first time in four games.
Mason McTavish has a point in six straight games.
The Blues’ Brandon Carlo played his 700th NHL game.
Filip Forsberg scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 16.
